full_story_part1_c1.canonical_text: You call me mad. No. Nervous, perhaps, but perfectly sane. My illness sharpened my senses, especially my hearing. I hear everything in heaven and earth. Listen to my calm voice, and judge for yourself. I loved the old man who shared my home. He had never hurt me; I wanted none of his money. But his eye! Pale blue, covered by a cloudy film—a vulture's eye. Whenever it turned towards me, my blood went cold. I had to be free of it.

full_story_part1_c2.canonical_text: For seven nights, at midnight, I lifted his latch. You should have seen my patience! I eased the door open so slowly he never stirred, then let one thin ray escape my lantern. The eye was always closed. So I could do nothing. You understand: I hated the eye, not the man. Each morning I kindly asked how he had slept. On the eighth night, I nearly laughed at my cleverness. Then my thumb slipped against the lantern's fastening.

full_story_part2_c1_k1.canonical_text: I stood motionless. For an hour he sat in bed, listening. At last he groaned softly. Not pain—terror. I knew that sound. I uncovered the lantern. Its narrow beam found the eye. Wide open. A low, quick beating reached me, like a watch wrapped in cotton. His heart! Faster it went, and louder. What if a neighbour heard?

full_story_part2_c1_k2.canonical_text: I rushed forward. He shrieked once. I dragged him down and pulled the heavy bed over him. Finally, the beating stopped. I checked his pulse. Nothing. I hid his body beneath three floorboards and fitted them back exactly. Not a mark! You could have searched all night. At four in the morning, three police officers knocked. A neighbour had heard a shriek.

full_story_part3_c1_k1.canonical_text: I welcomed them. A bad dream, I explained; the cry was mine. The old man was away in the country. I showed them every room, then brought chairs into his bedroom. I sat directly above the body. You see how little I feared? They chatted pleasantly. I smiled. Then my head began to ache. A ringing filled my ears—but no. That low, quick beating again.
